question: Should a key's right-click show the same ten curves as a segment's, or keep Premiere's six?
context: Your animate mock (2026-10-12) says a key and a segment both offer the same ten curves. Your keyframe tasks of 2026-09-23 asked for Premiere key menu. Today both exist, and Ease In on a key (slow arriving) is the opposite of Ease in on a segment (slow start).

options.label: One list everywhere: keys show the ten curves, Hold and Draw a Curve; Ease In, Ease Out and Bezier leave the key menu
options.summary: Right-click a key, a segment, a row or open the timeline bar and you see the same list. A curve chosen on a key shapes the stretch that leaves it, as your animate mock draws.
pros: One list to learn, as the animate mock says
No word means two things: Ease in always means a slow start
Shaped curves (back, elastic, steps) reach keys too
cons: Premiere users lose the key menu they know (Ease In, Ease Out, Bezier)
Ease in on a key now means slow leaving, not slow arriving
options.mitigation: Bezier is still reached by dragging a handle on the graph, and Draw a Curve covers any shape Premiere eases make.

options.label: Keys keep Premiere six, segments keep the ten curves; the bar shows the curves once a segment is picked
options.summary: Exactly as today. A key right-click reads Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In and Out, Hold, Bezier; a segment right-click and the bar with a segment picked read the ten curves.
pros: Matches your 2026-09-23 ask and Premiere key menu
cons: Two lists, and Ease In means opposite things in them
Departs from the animate mock line: the same ten curves everywhere
options.mitigation: A heading on each list (Key and Curve) so the menus at least say which one they are.
